audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed across layers: full phases[3..4].side said 'Skill' and phases[5..6].side said 'Veigar', while content win[0..6] all say 'Xerath' and the packet levelChart is Xerath on all seven rows.
audit.why: Xerath's Q (750), W (1000) and E (1050) all outrange every Veigar tool except Baleful Strike (1000); Veigar has no dash and Event Horizon is only 725 range, so Xerath controls spacing at every stage. Win rate 56.97% over 2547 games agrees.
audit.corrected: All seven rows to Xerath; the whys already describe Xerath winning those stages, so only side/rating move.

audit.why: Spikes are accurate: Lost Chapter mana sustain, level 6 Rite of the Arcane (130/115/100s), first-item Luden's, and Veigar's uncapped Phenomenal Evil scaling late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Event Horizon interrupts Rite of the Arcane. Xerath's R is flagged 'channel — interruptible' and Veigar's E is hardCC at 725 range; a cage clipped onto a channelling Xerath ends the ult.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it was absent from every field.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d with real numbers: Event Horizon 20/18.5/17/15.5/14s, Xerath E 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s, R 130/115/100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Event Horizon 20s/14s, Xerath E 13s, and the R-cancel rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under 'Hold E exclusively for the engage'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Trade at the range where his burst reaches' (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2). Both also referenced a 'dash' Veigar does not have.
audit.why: Body contradicted its own title, and Veigar has no gap-closer in his kit.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their titles using real ranges and cooldowns.

audit.why: matchup-lint reported MISGENDER / COPY_PASTE_BLEED / COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT / UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE / HEDGING on these fields; cooldowns and ranges taken from champ-data/_kits.
audit.corrected: Pronouns matched to the enemy champion; bled trade text replaced with field-specific advice; cooldown lines given real per-rank numbers.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 and 14s maxed, 725 range — only the edge stuns, and a miss buys you a full rotation. - Shocking Orb is 13s down at rank 1: keep it for his step-up. - Never start Rite of the Arcane with his cage available; Event Horizon stuns you out of the channel.

edits.before: Veigar spends Event Horizon (Cage) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane reaches 5000 units — snipe him walking, and never channel while Event Horizon is up.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Inside 725 units Event Horizon lands and Dark Matter plus Primordial Burst follow — poke from 1050 where only Baleful Strike reaches you.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Veigar wins by caging you at 725, dropping Dark Matter on the stun, and finishing with Primordial Burst on your missing health.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Your 13s Shocking Orb is the one thing that stops his walk-up into a 20s Event Horizon — spend it on his step, not on a wave you could poke.

notes: phases[3..6].why already described Xerath winning those stages, so the side flips were made without why edits (no self-contradiction introduced). content win[0..6] were already 'Xerath', so no paired win[N] edits exist to write — a before==after edit would be a no-op and would take the chart group down. tradeBad and dontsFull[0].d both reference a 'dash' Veigar does not have; tradeBad is quoted verbatim in breakdown.trading and report[3] as well, and all three could not be rewritten inside the length band without expansion — flagged rather than half-fixed.
